title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Futures turned cautious Wed morning (Nasdaq 100 futures -0.5%) ahead of Nvidia earnings, after Tuesday's close higher (S&P +0.3%, Nasdaq +0.6%, Dow +0.3%) despite Canada-U.S. trade tensions, as oil sank ~4% to $88.58/bbl and the 10-yr yield eased to 4.64%
Markets: Asia-Pacific stocks rebounded (MSCI APAC +0.3%); Samsung and SK Hynix gained while Tokyo Electron and Kioxia slipped as traders trimmed chip exposure ahead of Nvidia's print
Companies: Nvidia reports Q2 results after today's close - Street expects ~$91B revenue and $2.09 EPS, seen as the key test of the AI trade's durability
Companies: Dick's Sporting Goods plunged ~31% Tuesday after cutting its outlook on weak sneaker demand tied to its Foot Locker business, dragging Nike, lululemon, Under Armour and Target lower too
Companies: Anthropic is reportedly set to tell investors its potential revenue opportunity tops $30T, topping SpaceX's earlier $28.5T claim

Macro/Policy: Canada-U.S. trade war deepens - Canada's retaliatory tariffs (15%-50% on ~$20B of U.S. goods, doubling steel/aluminum duties to 50%) take effect Sept. 8; PM Carney says Canada is 'at war' with the U.S., and Trump has floated doubling Canadian auto tariffs to 50% in January

Macro/Policy: Today brings July PCE inflation (Fed's preferred gauge) plus personal income/spending data, with markets also bracing for new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote Friday - a rare same-week collision with Nvidia earnings
